agree.reason: For a GM who credits the renovation, the 7.9-to-8.2 rise before the work began is hard to dismiss, and the seven-week record gives a concrete reason to choose her over the outsider, though it may not fully outweigh his larger-hotel experience.

honest.reason: It drops the unsupported "main reason" claim and uses only real figures, but "while I was rebuilding" quietly suggests she caused the early gain, and "no learning period" overstates things given she has never run a budget.

works_the_facts.reason: It works out that nearly half the score gain came before the renovation and that training now takes about half as long, but it leaves turnover as raw counts (9 of 14, 5 of 14) instead of the stronger 64% to 36%.

right_comparison.reason: It compares the score before and after the renovation and turnover before and after her promotion, and it describes the outside candidate fairly, but it never says what hiring an outsider would mean in transition time for the team.

qualification.reason: The budget commitments are checkable (finance course within three months, weekly sessions with the controller), but they don't give a number to measure progress against or say what happens if she falls short.

objections.reason: It answers the renovation objection with the pre-renovation numbers, admits the budget gap and the outsider's experience, and doesn't raise objections the facts already answer.

fit.reason: It is a one-page memo addressed to the GM with clear sections, as the brief asked.
